collection_summary: Multi-hop instance built from the Wikidata SPARQL endpoint: landlocked African countries → their bordering countries → those neighbors' official languages. The universe of 16 landlocked African countries comes from Wikidata directly via the all-ranks P31 path (`p:P31/ps:P31 wd:Q123480`) plus the continent filter (P30=Q15). Borders are P47 (shares border with), filtered to P31=Q6256 (country) to exclude non-state entities. Official languages are P37 (official language). Result: 225 rows × 3 columns, with composite PK on all three columns so each (country, neighbor, language) triple is a distinct evaluable row.
source_coverage_notes: Single-source instance grounded entirely in Wikidata. The full universe of 16 landlocked African countries is recovered directly from Wikidata typing — no rows are supplemented. Row distribution is uneven by neighbor: South Africa (12 official languages including South African Sign Language) and Zimbabwe (Wikidata lists 16 official languages) account for the majority of rows for any landlocked country that borders them. Some neighbors are partially-recognized states (e.g., Somaliland, classified as Q6256 by Wikidata) — kept per Wikidata typing rather than excluded by political-recognition judgment. The 225-row total is the full closed-world Wikidata projection of this query.
decision_log: Chose multi_hop as the primary category because the data flow is a 3-link chain (landlocked → bordering → official-language) typical of recursive/chained-join semantics — exactly the stress that the multi_hop category targets. No secondary category assigned: the row shape is row-per-triple, not row-per-entity-with-multiple-attributes, so multi_attribute_projection does not fit. Composite PK on all three columns rather than (landlocked, neighbor) so each language is a distinct evaluable row, which produces more rows for confidence calibration. Chose Wikidata SPARQL (Tier A) over manual Wikipedia extraction because borders + official languages are well-typed Wikidata properties; the curation_protocol §4 explicitly recommends Tier A for multi_hop. The all-ranks P31 path was chosen for the landlocked-country universe clause specifically because some items (notably Rwanda, Q1037) record their `instance of: landlocked country` claim at normal rank rather than preferred rank, so the truthy `wdt:P31` path silently dropped them; the all-ranks path captures the same Wikidata claim regardless of rank ordering and yields the canonical 16-country set without any external supplementation. operation_type is 'join' to match the protocol/UI vocabulary for chained-join queries.
normalization_decisions: Country and language names follow Wikidata English labels (rdfs:label via the wikibase:label service). 'South African Sign Language' is kept verbatim as it is the Wikidata canonical label and one of South Africa's 12 official languages (statutorily added in 2023). 'Democratic Republic of the Congo' is kept full-form (not abbreviated 'DRC') per the curation_protocol §6 country normalization rule. The label service produced no unresolved QID fallback rows. The composite PK uses exact-string-match across all three columns; the evaluator must compare full canonical names.
open_questions: 1) South Africa's 12 official languages and Zimbabwe's 16 inflate row counts for any landlocked country that borders them, which means the per-country evaluation signal will be dominated by these two neighbors. Down-weighting strategies (e.g., evaluate per (landlocked, neighbor) pair rather than per triple) are a downstream metric question, not a curation issue. 2) Some neighbors are partially-recognized states (e.g., Somaliland classified as Q6256). Kept by Wikidata typing rather than judged separately. If a future repair wants to exclude partially-recognized states, document that policy here and re-run with a stricter filter (e.g., exclude entities with Q15634554 'state with limited recognition'). 3) Wikidata's P37 may include languages with limited regional or de jure status (e.g., national vs. official distinction). For this instance, P37 was taken at face value as 'official language' per Wikidata convention. 4) The all-ranks P31 path is sensitive to Wikidata rank-curation choices: if a future Wikidata edit demotes a Q123480 statement to deprecated rank, this query will still include it. Periodic re-runs should compare the count against the expected 16.
